subject: Why does document() recompile C/C++ code

messages.author: deea3c30b4c8409f
messages.subject: Why does document() recompile C/C++ code
parts:
Hi,

I have a package with a lot C/C++ files, and each time I call `document()`, they are recompiled. The C/C++ sources are not changing, there is no Rcpp attributes or anything like that involved. Even if I just modify an R file, and then call `document()`, the sources are recompiled.

Am I doing something wrong? 

Is this something that can be fixed? If yes, I am willing to look into it, just want to know first if there is something to fix.

Thanks,
Gabor

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Why does document() recompile C/C++ code
parts:
document() calls load_all(), so I'd try to figure out why load_all()
recompiles each time - it should do everything in place.
Hadley

messages.author: deea3c30b4c8409f
messages.subject: Re: Why does document() recompile C/C++ code
parts:
OK, the thing is, `R CMD install` runs `configure`, and then
`configure` (re)creates `Makevars`, and that triggers a rebuild. So I
guess this generally comes up with packages that have `configure`
scripts.

So one way to avoid this is to make `configure` only overwrite files
if they really change. I'll include the code here, in case somebody
else has this problem. So instead of the typical

AC_CONFIG_FILES([src/Makevars])

you need something like

AC_CONFIG_FILES([src/Makevars.tmp:src/Makevars.in], [
if test -f src/Makevars && cmp -s src/Makevars.tmp src/Makevars; then
AC_MSG_NOTICE([creating src/Makevars])
AC_MSG_NOTICE([src/Makevars is unchanged])
rm src/Makevars.tmp
else
AC_MSG_NOTICE([creating src/Makevars])
mv src/Makevars.tmp src/Makevars
fi
]
)

Which will only create/overwrite `src/Makevars` if it does not exist,
or it is different. If you create multiple config files from
`configure`, then you can write an autoconf macro for this.

Gabor
